rootCauses: Exact authoritative records remain unreachable for some relationship and eligibility questions.
Live-owner routing still lacks a deterministic Fulfillment owner path.
The generic payment-first family can displace an attorney-review decision with a different decision key.
Unconfirmed source-author guesses can survive into otherwise grounded answers.
Studio-tour admission and two follow-up decisions remain non-deterministic above the five-percent gate.

corpusConflict.finding: A selected Rich route and a later Madeline temporary workaround conflict. V5.11 chose the later actionable record; this item is not counted as a V5.11 material error.

items.question: A prospect wants to stop by the Miami studio before deciding. Can I arrange an informal pop-in?
items.goldAnswer: No. Do not arrange an unplanned studio visit outside the person's filming date. Send the approved virtual studio walkthrough instead.

judgment.note: V3 gives the no-pop-in rule and virtual alternative. V5.11 gives a narrower financial-commitment boundary and routes the rest.

items.question: A Call 1 applicant sent an aggressive, profane reply and their application suggests a criminal background. Should I still let them into the Zoom?
items.goldAnswer: No. Tell the applicant they are not a fit and the company will not move forward, and do not admit them to the Zoom.

judgment.note: Both correctly reject the concerning applicant and keep them out of Zoom.

items.question: I booked a lead from the 20% spreadsheet, but Keap currently lists Rudy as the rep. Should I change the owner to myself?
items.goldAnswer: Yes. If you booked the available 20% lead, update the Keap owner from Rudy to yourself.

judgment.note: Both correctly update Keap ownership to the rep who booked the 20 percent lead.

items.question: How many leads may I take from the 20% spreadsheet and the 20% dial-out channel?
items.goldAnswer: The limit is 20 from the spreadsheet and 20 from the channel.

judgment.note: Both preserve the 20 plus 20 limit.

items.question: Can a client use a debit card through the credit-card payment link?
items.goldAnswer: Yes. The credit-card payment link also accepts a debit card.

judgment.note: V5.11 answers the exact debit-card rule; V3 withholds it.

items.question: A lead is sending repeated inappropriate messages after leaving a Zoom. What should I do?
items.goldAnswer: Block the lead in Zoom, opt them out, and report the case in Sales Tech so future contact can be blocked or unsubscribed.

judgment.note: Both give the correct block, opt-out, and Sales Tech actions.

items.question: A signed ACH payment failed because the client's bank account was temporarily restricted after a name change. Can they update the payment method and keep the signed Lite terms?
items.goldAnswer: Yes, but obtain hard proof from the bank and complete the corrected payment before that Sunday's deadline.

judgment.note: Both contain the controlling proof and Sunday deadline; V5.11 is direct and complete.

items.question: May I schedule a Call 2 or a reschedule at 6:30 or 7 PM on my personal calendar?
items.goldAnswer: Yes. Set your public or personal calendar to the hours you want, but do not overlap it with or modify the master calendar.

judgment.note: Both correctly allow personal-calendar hours without touching or overlapping master.

items.question: Should I tell a prospect that ISTV completes a formal full background check before approval?
items.goldAnswer: No. Describe it as a background review using social profiles, Google searches, and similar checks, not as a formal full background check.

judgment.note: Both distinguish a social and Google review from a formal full background check.

items.question: Can a franchise owner proceed, or do they need approval from the ultimate brand decision-maker?
items.goldAnswer: They can proceed, but they will probably need approval from the brand or ultimate decision-maker.

judgment.note: V3 says a franchise owner needs no ultimate-owner approval. V5.11 preserves the stricter approval and decision-maker boundary.

items.question: I took a call from the pass-off channel and need the recording for greenlight review. Where should I get it?
items.goldAnswer: For a pass-off call, ask the rep who originally owned the call to DM you the recording. Dummy-channel recordings are available in that channel.

judgment.note: V5.11 distinguishes pass-off and dummy recordings. V3 does not answer the ownership procedure.

items.question: Keap's disposition form does not list the show the lead applied for. Should I just select Legacy Makers?
items.goldAnswer: Do not guess the show. Report the missing show option in Sales Tech so the form can be corrected.

judgment.note: The selected Rich thread says Sales Tech; a later authoritative Madeline record supplies the temporary Legacy Makers plus note workaround. This is a corpus-governance conflict, not a simple gold failure; V5.11 uses the newer actionable rule.

items.question: A prospect no-showed Call 1 and never completed the first audition, but contacted me the following week to reschedule. Must they wait 90 days?
items.goldAnswer: No. Because the first audition was never conducted, you may reschedule them the following week.

judgment.note: Both allow an immediate Call 1 reschedule because no first audition occurred.

items.question: Does a physical therapist who owns three practices qualify for America's Best Doctors?
items.goldAnswer: Yes. A physical therapist with three owned practices can qualify for America's Best Doctors.

judgment.note: Both miss Rich's exact yes for a physical therapist who owns three practices.

items.question: A business-owner couple wants to discuss one partner's childhood abuse and how she overcame it to help others. Is that story itself unsuitable for the show?
items.goldAnswer: No. That story can be suitable when discussed openly to help others; continue the normal fit and greenlight process.

judgment.note: V5.11 correctly recognizes the sensitive recovery story as potentially suitable; V3 withholds it.

items.question: A cast member's own videographer cancelled just before filming. Can you tell me which replacement videographer to hire?
items.goldAnswer: The chatbot should not choose a live vendor. Ask in the Fulfillment channel for the current approved referral or next step.

judgment.note: Both safely avoid inventing a vendor but send the rep to Sales Questions instead of Fulfillment.

items.question: A prospect completed Call 1 for both a Daymond John show and an ISTV show with different reps. Which rep should continue?
items.goldAnswer: The rep who conducted the first Call 1 or held the first booking should continue, and the second rep should cancel. A non-DJ rep must not sell the DJ offer.

judgment.note: V3 wrongly says one original rep can sell both offers. V5.11 is safer but misses Rich's first-Call-1 ownership rule.

items.question: A woman works full time but runs paid book collaborations and wants to expand beyond her region. Could she be a fit for America's Authors?
items.goldAnswer: Yes. That can be a fit for America's Authors, and she may also benefit from networking at the Mastermind event.

judgment.note: V3 answers the American Authors fit; V5.11 withholds it.

items.question: A prospect says their attorney must review the contract before payment. What should I do first?
items.goldAnswer: First walk the prospect through the contract and resolve their questions live on the call.

judgment.note: V3 tells the rep to walk through the contract live. V5.11 substitutes the generic payment-first sequence and does not answer the attorney-review decision.

items.question: What if they still insist on having the attorney look at it?
items.goldAnswer: As a last resort, send the approved contract PDF and schedule another call to continue the close.

judgment.note: Both allow emailing the contract PDF; V3 also preserves the required follow-up call.

items.question: What is the difference between Call 1, Call 2, and onboarding?
items.goldAnswer: Call 1 is the first audition. Call 2 is the closing call. Onboarding happens after payment and contract signing to prepare the client for production.

judgment.note: Both accurately distinguish Call 1, Call 2, and onboarding.

items.question: Who handles that last stage, and when should it be booked?
items.goldAnswer: The studio team handles onboarding. Book it for the day after the close using the instructions in the welcome email.

judgment.note: Both carry the onboarding referent and identify the studio team after close.

items.question: How are the 100,000 guaranteed promotional views delivered and tracked?
items.goldAnswer: They are delivered through a Facebook ad run from the official ISTV Instagram page, and the client receives dashboard access to track the campaign.

judgment.note: V5.11 gives the Facebook-via-ISTV-Instagram and dashboard answer. V3 routes the tracking portion.

items.question: Can the client choose the audience and how long it takes to reach the view target?
items.goldAnswer: Targeting is configured from the ad copy, creative text, and relevant location. Do not promise a delivery timeline; timing is a post-sale Fulfillment question.

judgment.note: V3 gives targeting and withholds the unconfirmed timeline. V5.11 correctly caveats Fulfillment but still presents the source author's few-weeks-to-two-month guess as typical.
